sections.title: How our projects will evolve
sections.body:
| Project | Application | Engineering objective |
|--------|--------|--------|
| P1 | Intelligent tool-calling assistant | Understand agent execution loops |
| P2 | Research and analysis agent | Planning and evidence gathering |
| P3 | Persistent personal assistant | Memory and context management |
| P4 | Customer-support agent | Routing, state and escalation |
| P5 | Multi-agent document analyst | Agent collaboration |
| P6 | MCP-enabled enterprise assistant | External tool integration |
| P7 | Finance and procurement agent | Approval and transaction safety |
| P8 | Autonomous IT support agent | Fault tolerance and remediation |
| P9 | Agent observability platform | Evaluation, tracing and monitoring |
| P10 | Enterprise agentic AI platform | Complete production deployment |

diagram.title: Visual flow — How our projects will evolve

steps.label: Orchestrator
steps.narration: A coordinator decomposes work and assigns ownership to specialists.

steps.label: Delegate
steps.narration: Tasks are handed off with clear inputs, outputs, and termination conditions.

steps.label: Specialists
steps.narration: Specialist agents execute narrow skills and return structured results.

steps.label: Merge
steps.narration: Results are reconciled; conflicts and duplicates are resolved before final output.

steps.label: Terminate
steps.narration: The workflow must always end — via success, safe failure, timeout, or human decision.
